evidence_quote: Eligible participants met the following two criteria: (a) a school designation of LEP or an LEP designation in the previous 5 years and (b) a score of 1,612 or below on the eighth-grade reading portion of the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR).
resolved_title: Efficacy of a High School Extensive Reading Intervention for English Learners With Reading Difficulties (Vaughn, Martinez, Williams, Miciak, Fall, and Roberts; Journal of Educational Psychology; ERIC ED586763)
notes: Student rule is an EL designation plus a STAAR reading cutoff (score at or below 1,612, one SE above the failing score), so tie-breaker 1 gives targeted_low; schools were also chosen for having many ELs, so level = both. Students were screened and randomized before consent, no sign-up, opt_in = 0. Document identity doubt: this text is a grade 9 to 10 high school trial (358 enrolled of 713 randomized, 264 with complete data), but Kraft lists grades 4-5 and n = 252, and the text was matched to ERIC by title only. Kraft may have cited a different Vaughn et al. 2019 paper (a grade 4 to 5 reading-difficulties trial), which is why mixed_samples = 1 and confidence is medium rather than high; a reviewer should confirm which document Kraft used.

evidence_quote: Students who were identified as English language learners (ELLs) and were eligible for mainstreaming were randomly assigned to classrooms participating in the study.
resolved_title: WWC Review of the Report: A Randomized Experiment of a Cognitive Strategies Approach to Text-Based Analytical Writing for Mainstreamed Latino English Language Learners in Grades 6 to 12 (WWC Single Study Review, August 2012; ERIC ED534781)
notes: The text file is the WWC single study review of Kim et al. (2011), not the JREE article itself; the WWC sample text in wwc-codes.csv agrees (2,726 English learners in grades 6 to 12, Santa Ana USD). Selection was on EL status with no achievement cutoff (mainstreaming eligibility is a language-proficiency status), so targeted_other per tie-breaker 4. Confidence medium: the eligibility statement is explicit and the article title names the population, but the source is a WWC summary rather than the article full text. Kraft lists three effects (0.07, 0.20, 0.05), grades 4-11, and n up to 4,459; only the 0.05 CST reading effect and the grade 6 to 12 range match this trial (n = 2,711 to 2,721), so at least one of Kraft effects appears to come from a different Pathway Project sample or report, hence mixed_samples = 1. Related row 485-olson-2012 covers the same project.

evidence_quote: It focused on school districts that had low student achievement and large proportions of students in poverty, but these were general guidelines rather than strict eligibility criteria. [...] Generally, schools were identified by senior district staff based on broad considerations including whether schools had adequate technology infrastructure and whether schools were participating in other initiatives.
resolved_title: Effectiveness of Reading and Mathematics Software Products: Findings From Two Student Cohorts (NCEE 2009-4041; Campuzano, Dynarski, Agodini, and Rall, 2009; ERIC ED504657)
notes: Judgment call. District recruitment was deliberately aimed at low achievement and poverty (tie-breaker 1 makes achievement plus poverty targeted_low, level = school), and the report documents the resulting skew (FRL 57 to 60 percent in math districts versus 36 percent nationally). But the report itself says these were general guidelines rather than strict eligibility criteria, schools were picked by district staff on infrastructure and other initiatives, teachers volunteered, and students were allocated to classrooms in the usual way with no student rule; a reviewer could defensibly code universal under tie-breaker 6. Confidence medium for that reason. Kraft used the second-year math results (sixth grade math products PLATO Achieve Now and Larson Pre-Algebra; algebra I products Cognitive Tutor and Larson Algebra I); n_min 276 matches the Cognitive Tutor second-year sample, exact product pairing for the two effects (-0.06, 0.00) not confirmed. Teacher volunteering is not student opt-in, so opt_in = 0.
